experiments.hypothesis: Daily rainfall cannot express burst intensity: 100 mm in 4 h and 100 mm spread over 24 h give features/rainfall.py::_id_ratio the IDENTICAL value, and the published ID curve it encodes is TRMM-derived at D ~ 3-6 h, so at D = 24 h it is far outside its calibration domain. Phase A measured the symptom -- FN share on an apparently dry day is 0.635. Exposing worst 1/3/6/12 h bursts in the preceding 24 h and 72 h should recover positives the daily view reads as dry. X6 minus X5 isolates the sub-daily contribution.

experiments.hypothesis: The real Phase B test. X6 found ERA5 sub-daily adds nothing beyond ERA5 daily (X6-X5 = -0.0015, inside a 0.0084 floor), but that null was PRE-REGISTERED as ambiguous: ERA5 is reanalysis at 0.25 deg and this repo's own 10_chirps.sh documents it under-representing orographic Himalayan extremes -- exactly the bursts being tested. IMERG is satellite-based, 0.1 deg, half-hourly, built for precipitation extremes. If X8-X7 also lands inside the A/A floor, sub-daily intensity is closed from two independent products and daily granularity is not the constraint. If X8-X7 is real where X6-X5 was not, the ERA5 null was ERA5's own extreme-rainfall limitation, exactly as the caveat predicted.
